query: Lee Jae-myung approval rating Gallup Korea Realmeter late June early July 2026, is approval still falling, what is driving the decline, any dead cross
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the key takeaway on your question:

**Is approval still falling?** No longer, as of the latest data. Approval bottomed out in mid-to-late June 2026 after a ~6-week decline, then **rebounded in both pollsters** in early-to-mid July.

**Dead cross?** Yes — but **only in Realmeter**, which recorded Lee's first-ever dead cross on June 22, 2026 (46.7% approval vs 49.7% disapproval), persisting through late June. By July 13 (48.9% vs 47.7%), it had effectively reversed. **Gallup never showed a dead cross** — its low was 51% approval, recovering to 54% by July 3.

**What drove the decline:** NEC ballot-mishandling controversy from the June 3 local elections, economic/livelihood concerns ("excessive" welfare/spending), Democratic Party infighting, and prosecutorial reform disputes.

**What drove the rebound:** NATO summit diplomacy/security achievements (Realmeter) and the "three mega projects" semiconductor/AI investment initiative (Gallup).

Full structured findings with all data points and sources have been submitted.

key_facts: Realmeter recorded Lee Jae-myung's FIRST dead cross since inauguration on June 22, 2026: approval 46.7% vs disapproval 49.7% (June 15-19 fieldwork).
Realmeter June 29 release (June 22-26 fieldwork): approval 46.5%, disapproval 49.5% - sixth consecutive weekly decline, second straight week in dead cross.
Realmeter rebound by July 13 release (July 8-12 fieldwork): approval 48.9% (+1.9pp), disapproval 47.7% (-1.5pp) - second straight weekly rise, dead cross reversed.
Gallup Korea low was 51% approval (June 24-26 survey), the lowest since Lee took office June 2025 - but NO dead cross.
Gallup recovery: June 30-July 2 survey (released July 3) showed approval 54% (+3pp), disapproval 36% (-5pp).
Gallup never registered a dead cross; Realmeter did (June 22-early July 2026).
Decline drivers: NEC ballot mishandling in June 3 local elections, economic/livelihood concerns, Democratic Party infighting, prosecutorial reform disputes.
Rebound drivers: NATO summit diplomacy/security achievements and the government's 'three mega projects' (semiconductor/AI, balanced regional development).
Realmeter party support (July 8-12): Democratic Party 44.8% (+1.8pp), People Power Party 38.1% (-2.2pp).
As of latest data (mid-July 2026), approval was rising, not falling, in both Gallup and Realmeter series.
